# Trichy assault rifle

The **Trichy assault rifle** (TAR), sometimes known as the **Tiruchi assault rifle**, is an Indian-made assault rifle chambered for the 7.62×39mm round . It is manufactured by Ordnance Factory Tiruchirappalli (OFT) and is based on the Bulgarian AR-M1, itself a licensed copy of the Kalashnikov AKM . The rifle has gained significant acceptance among Indian paramilitary forces and police departments as a cost-effective indigenous alternative to imported weapons .

## Development and design

### Background and development timeline

The development of the Trichy assault rifle began in 2015 at Ordnance Factory Tiruchirappalli . To mark the contribution of the Tiruchi factory in developing the rifle, officials decided to christen it "Trichy assault rifle" . The production line was established in 2017, and the rifle was first unveiled in May 2011 .

The TAR is a wholly indigenous copy of the AK-47, developed using experience gained from mass-producing licensed versions of the weapon . The full-sized TAR is believed to be a copy of the Bulgarian AR-M1, itself a licensed copy of the Kalashnikov . Over 500,000 Bulgarian weapons had been imported by India's central, state, and paramilitary forces over the previous decade, and the TAR has helped reduce imports from that East European country .

### Technical specifications

The 7.62×39mm Trichy Assault Rifle is a powerful individual automatic weapon designed to destroy the enemy by fire in single and burst firing modes . It is a single-shot rifle in normal mode and can be used in burst mode as well. By firing in burst mode in short series, group or single targets at a range up to 500 meters can be destroyed, though the destructive effect of the TAR extends up to a range of 1,350 meters .

The rifle features:

* **Caliber**: 7.62×39mm

* **Action**: Gas-operated, rotating bolt

* **Rate of fire**: 600 rounds per minute (full automatic)

* **Muzzle velocity**: 710–715 m/s (2,330–2,350 ft/s)

* **Effective firing range**: 300–350 meters (TAR)

* **Weight**: 3.4 kg (7.5 lb) (TAR); 3.17 kg (7.0 lb) (TriCa carbine)

* **Length**: 900 mm (35 in) with folding stock extended; 650 mm (25.6 in) with stock folded (for the down-folding variant)

* **Barrel length**: Varies by variant

### Design features

The TAR has several notable design features. It has a monoblock receiver, shockproof polymer lower parts, and two Picatinny rails that can mount a variety of sights and scopes . One of the significant features is a chrome-plated bore and six-groove rifling .

The rifle uses the AK-47's distinctive 30-round curved box magazine and features commonality of parts with existing weapons . This design choice eases logistics as the ammunition is in widespread production and use .

## Variants

### Standard variants

Ordnance Factory Tiruchirappalli manufactures TAR rifles in multiple variants :

1. **Fixed butt version** - The standard configuration

2. **Side-folding butt version** - Allows for compact storage and transport

3. **Down-folding butt version** - Launched on August 25, 2021, in commemoration of 75 years of Indian independence

The down-folding butt version was developed to meet customer requirements as some Central Armed Police Force (CAPF) units, State Police, and Railway Protection Force (RPF) required this version for quick and easy movement of personnel in guard and patrolling duty .

### Compact variants

#### TriCa carbine

The TriCa (Trichy Carbine) is a lighter and compact 7.62×39mm carbine designed for infantry combat vehicle crew, helicopter crew, and security personnel for operations that call for a compact and relatively powerful individual automatic weapon . It is also suitable for paratroopers, police, and security personnel guarding highly secure facilities such as airports, and for use by Special Operation Forces .

The TriCa has a special muzzle booster that helps in hiding the flash and mitigating the sound when fired . An advantage is that it can use ammunition and magazines as well as interchangeable parts of general assault rifles (TAR and AK-47) . The carbine can be concealed in clothes and hidden in the jackets of security personnel .

#### Baby TAR/TAR-3

The "Baby TAR" (TAR-3) is India's smallest assault rifle, developed as a compact, fully automatic version of the Trichy Assault Rifle . It fires the same 7.62×39mm cartridge as the AK-47 and uses the AK-47's 30-round curved box magazine .

The Baby TAR features:

* **Barrel length**: 8.3 inches (chopped down from the AK-47's 16-inch barrel)

* **Effective range**: 150 meters

* **Length with stock folded**: 19.2 inches 

* **Weight (unloaded)**: 2.7 kg (1 kg lighter than the AK-47) 

The weapon has a monoblock receiver, shockproof polymer lower parts, and two Picatinny rails that can mount a variety of sights and scopes . Its designers say it is ideal for special forces and counter-terrorist operators who want compact, concealable weapons but with the firepower of a full-sized AK-47. The assault rifle is also suitable for aircraft, tank, and vehicle crews .

## Production and service history

### Production capacity

Ordnance Factory Tiruchirappalli has established significant production capacity for the TAR. The factory has a monthly output rate of 2,000 TAR rifles . This production capability has enabled the factory to fulfill large orders from various security forces across India.

### Service adoption

The Trichy assault rifle has been widely adopted by various Indian security forces:

1. **Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF)**:

* Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) 

* Border Security Force (BSF)

* Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB)

* Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP)

* Central Industrial Security Force (CISF)

1. **State police forces**:

* Kerala Police

* Police forces in states dealing with Naxalite insurgency

* Police forces in Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Jharkhand, and Chhattisgarh 

1. **Other organizations**:

* Railway Protection Force (RPF)

* National Security Guard (NSG) - ordered 100 TriCa carbines in December 2021

### Notable orders

Recent significant orders include:

* On February 12, 2022, the CRPF placed a large order for 10,000 TAR costing 76.48 crore with Advance Weapons & Equipment India Limited (AWEIL)

* On January 31, 2022, AWEIL received an order from Kerala Police for 92 TriCa carbines costing 67.16 crore

### Delivery statistics

According to unclassified reports from the Department of Defense, out of the orders for 78,000 guns placed collectively by various forces, OFT has delivered 30,000 Tiruchi Assault Rifle (TAR) and will supply 42,000 to 45,000 units during the fiscal year . OFT has provided around 10,000 rifles to Central Armed Police Forces such as the BSF, SSB, ITBP, and CISF .

The Central Armed Police Forces' faith in the assault rifle points to its success . Nearly 20,000 weapons have been delivered to Indian police, paramilitary, and central armed police forces .

## Cost and advantages

The Trichy assault rifle offers significant cost advantages over imported alternatives. Each TAR costs around Rs 55,000, which is far less than the licensed AK-203 to be produced by Indo-Russian Rifles, which will cost upwards of Rs 75,000 .

The rifle's design offers several advantages:

1. **Logistics efficiency**: Uses widely available 7.62×39mm ammunition and AK-47 pattern magazines

2. **Parts commonality**: Shares interchangeable parts with existing AK-47 variants 

3. **Indigenous production**: Reduces dependence on foreign imports and supports India's Atmanirbhar Bharat (self-reliant India) initiative

4. **Proven reliability**: Based on the well-proven AK-47 design with 本土化 improvements 

## Technical innovations

Designers at OF Trichy have solved a significant technical challenge that stumped gun designers of the DRDO's now-discarded INSAS carbine variant in the 1990s—how to reduce barrel heating and excessive sound and flash produced when an assault rifle bullet is fired from a short barrel .

The Baby TAR designers solved this problem by using internal metal reflectors to insulate the foregrip from the barrel and by designing an in-house compact flash hider at the barrel muzzle . The gun can presently fire four full magazines (around 120 rounds) without the barrel overheating . This development is noteworthy because it means Indian designers now understand the "know-why," rather than just the "know-how" that they would have gained from licensed production .

## Conclusion

The Trichy assault rifle represents a significant achievement in India's small arms manufacturing capabilities. As an indigenous alternative to imported weapons, it has successfully met the requirements of various security forces across the country. With its cost-effective production, reliable performance, and 不断 expanding range of variants, the TAR has become an important component of India's defense and security infrastructure.

The rifle's success is evident in the large orders placed by multiple agencies and its growing adoption by state police forces. The continued development of variants such as the TriCa carbine and Baby TAR demonstrates the ongoing innovation at Ordnance Factory Tiruchirappalli, supporting India's goal of self-reliance in defense manufacturing.

Ordnance Factory Tiruchy hands over 500 assault rifles to CRPF
==============================================================

Ordnance Factory Tiruchy (OFT) on Thursday handed over the first consignment of 500 assault rifles to CRPF.
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

From our online archive

Updated:13th Mar, 2020 at 5:33 PM

TIRUCHY: Ordnance Factory Tiruchy (OFT) on Thursday handed over the first consignment of 500 assault rifles to CRPF. Trichy Assault Rifles or TAR, as these are called, are the indigenous version of AK-47 rifle. Shirish Khare, GM, OFT handed over the rifles to DS Rawat, DIG, CRPF.

OFT started the development of the rifle in 2015, and established a production line in 2017. The first batch of 200 TARs was delivered to Chandigarh police in March 2017. In November 2017, the CRPF tested the rifle for functionality and reliability. It was subjected to a life cycle test by firing 15,000 rounds in one go. In February 2018, the TAR was deployed for a field trial at Jagdalpur, Raipur, Guwahati and Srinagar. Following this, order for 6167 rifles were placed.

OFT would supply TARs in both fixed and foldable butt models, sources said adding that the latter was in the development stage. The TAR is compatible with GP-25, 30 and UBGL M-6 grenade launchers.

OFT has so far supplied more than 10,000 rifles to Central Armed Police Forces including the BSF, SSB, ITBP & CISF. Police force in several States have also inducted TAR under their modernisation scheme.

OFT has also taken up research and development projects such as the trial of 7.62X39mm TAR Carbine(long barrel firearm) and 40X46mm UBGL (Underbarrel Grenade

Launcher) for TAR/AK 47, which after induction would serve as an import substitute.

Nagpur: Even as the AK-203, the latest version of the dreaded Kalashnikov rifle, will be made in India in collaboration with the Russians, a comparable fully indigenous rifle has also been developed, and is already in use. The Indian weapon will be on display at the Defence Expo in Lucknow starting February 5. Known as the Trichy Assault Rifle (TAR), after Ordnance Factory Tiruchirapally (OFT), where it is made, the Indian rifle claims to be at par in terms of functionality with the Kalashnikov.

![Image 3: 1x1 polls](https://static.toiimg.com/photo/25581306.cms)

Information gathered by TOI says the AK-203 has an added feature of Picatiny rails, which can be used to fix reflexer or laser designator. Sources say the rails can be put in TAR too, and are basically add-ons. The TAR, which is made of solid metal, is also fundamentally said to be sturdier than the AK-203, which is made of sheet metal. Lately, there has been a shift to solid body in rifles in other countries too, said sources.

The AK-203 will be made at Ordnance Factory Korwa in Uttar Pradesh’s Amethi district by Indo Russian Rifle Private Limited (IRRPL), for the Indian army. The IRRPL, which is a joint venture between Russia’s Kalashnikov Concern and the Ordnance Factory Board (OFB), has a mandate to make over 7 lakh rifles. The agreement is an outcome of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s visit to Russia last year.

Now as an inter-government deal has been struck between Russia and India, the Army would be going ahead with the Kalashnikovs. TAR, on the other hand, is being pushed for the paramilitary forces, which are already buying it. The deal gives a major boost Russia’s Kalashnikov Concern for entering the Indian market. OFB sees the TAR as the means to regain its trust, which it lost over the Insas rifle. OFB, which had drawn flak over its plan to corporatize the set up as a revamp move, is hoping to continue with orders from the paramilitary, with even the AK-203 being manufactured parallelly.

The production is to start in a year, as OFT has already begun making the TAR. This year, the factory has an order for nearly 40,000 pieces from the central paramilitary forces coming under the ministry of home affairs (MHA). CRPF is the major buyer. 

A comparative analysis using data accessed by TOI shows that TAR, AK-47, and AK-203 have the same rate of fire at 600 rounds a minute, and muzzle velocity of 700 to 715m/s. All the three rifles can hit up to an effective range of over 350 meters. 

The range depends on the length of the barrel and calibre of ammunition. The three guns have a barrel length of 415mm and use ammunition of 7.62x39 mm calibre. The ammunition will be made at the Ordnance Factory Warangaon, near Bhusawal, and will also be used for the AK-203 after it is inducted in the Army.

The range also meets the Army’s specifications for the assault rifle it needs, said sources. Even the picatiny rails that are in the AK-203, are being put in TAR on the basis of orders, a source said. 

TAR was also offered to the Army initially, which had reverted with demand for a few corrections, said sources requesting anonymity. In the meantime, the gun was accepted by the paramilitary forces. TAR is now set to replace the Bulgarian AK-47 made by Arsenal Joint Stock Company, from where the paramilitary has been mainly sourcing its rifles.

Over 15,000 rounds were fired to test the TAR’s life cycle and over 2,400 for reliability, said sources. The trials were carried out at the CRPF Academy in Gurgaon after which a final approval was given. With more orders in sight, the ordnance factory is planning to increase production capacity at Tiruchirapally.

After the Army rejected the 5.56 Insas rifle, which was also used during the Kargil war, OFB preferred to eye paramilitary forces instead, said sources. Apart from operational issues reported in the Insas, the Army did not prefer it because Insas having a smaller ammunition of 5.56mm did not have the lethality, It would rather injure the enemy than kill.

Earlier, the Army had preferred the 5.56mm ammunition going by the theory that an injured enemy is of more use than a dead one. Later, considering the requirement in counter-insurgency areas, it was decided to have the 7.26mm round for which TAR was made.

Ordnance Factory Tiruchirappalli Launched A Variant Of TriCa With Down Folding Butt
===================================================================================

[![Image 7: Photo of Shankul Bhandare](https://www.defencexp.com/wp-content/litespeed/avatar/5cdc49aaa26c62ae4a4aee49071cc118.jpg?ver=1766217098)](https://www.defencexp.com/author/shankulchandrashekharbhandre/)[Shankul Bhandare](https://www.defencexp.com/author/shankulchandrashekharbhandre/ "Shankul Bhandare")[Follow on X](https://twitter.com/itz_shankul?s=09 "Follow on X")[Send an email](mailto:Shankul.sb@gmail.com "Send an email")August 26, 2021

0 438  1 minute read

![Image 8: Ordnance Factory Tiruchirappalli Launched A Variant Of TriCa With Down Folding Butt](https://i0.wp.com/www.defencexp.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/08/Untitled-design-2-min-37.png?fit=1200%2C675&ssl=1)

A high-tech, low sound carbine named ‘TriCa’ with down folding butt with a range of more effective than a typical submachine gun and small enough to be packed in the jacket of security personnel was unveiled at the[Ordnance Factory](https://www.defencexp.com/246-year-old-ordnance-factory-board-to-be-scrapped/)in Tiruchirappalli,[Tamil Nadu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamil_Nadu), during the function held on 25th August 2021.

> In continuation to the launch of TriCa (Trichy Carbine) and 40 X 46 mm UBGL for TAR and AK-47 ,as a part of Atma Nirbhar Bharath, Ordnance Factory Tiruchirappalli launched a variant of 7.62X39 mm TAR with Down Folding Butt during the function held on 25th August 2021. @OFB_India [pic.twitter.com/OF4vYXouB9](https://t.co/OF4vYXouB9)
> 
> — PRO-OFT (@OftPro) [August 25, 2021](https://twitter.com/OftPro/status/1430530197455990792?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

The lighter and compact weapon, the 7.62X39 mm carbine TriCa is designed for the infantry combat vehicle, helicopter crew, and security personnel for operations that call for a compact and relatively powerful individual automatic weapon.

*   ![Image 9: The Ordnance Factory Trichy is launching the 7.62x39mm TAR Down Folding Butt Version on August 25, 2021](https://i0.wp.com/www.defencexp.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/08/E9pCtmpVcAEufJc-1.jpg?resize=708%2C344&ssl=1)
*   ![Image 10: A 2x1 image, likely be a tacker probe](https://i0.wp.com/www.defencexp.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/08/Untitled-design-1-min-77.png?resize=708%2C398&ssl=1)

[](https://www.defencexp.com/ordnance-factory-tiruchirappalli-launched-a-variant-of-trica-with-down-folding-butt/)[](https://www.defencexp.com/ordnance-factory-tiruchirappalli-launched-a-variant-of-trica-with-down-folding-butt/)[](https://www.defencexp.com/ordnance-factory-tiruchirappalli-launched-a-variant-of-trica-with-down-folding-butt/)

The weapon is also for paratroopers, police, and security personnel guarding highly secure facilities such as airports, and for use by the Special Operation Forces.

TriCa has a special muzzle booster that helps in hiding the flash and mitigating the sound when fired, the release said.

An advantage is that it can use ammunition and magazines as well as the interchangeable parts of general assault rifles (TAR and AK-47).

The carbine could be concealed in clothes and hidden in the jackets of security personnel.

It was developed by the in-house research and development unit of the Ordnance Factory.

该枪就是保加利亚arm1突击步枪的印度仿制品，并为该枪研发了枪挂榴弹发射器，也是保加利亚的仿制品。生产该枪时俄罗斯还提出了严重的抗议。

是一种单兵自动武器，该枪可以单射也可以连发。可以摧毁最远 500m 范围内的目标。然而，该枪的最大射程可达 1350m。

该枪由固定枪托 伸缩枪托 折叠枪托三种组成，折叠枪托和保加利亚的枪托一模一样。折叠枪托的总长度在对接打开状态下为 900 毫米，在折叠状态下为 650 毫。

不过这枪的命运比较好，本国警察部队买得多，下来10万支，口碑也不错。客户如伞兵部队，中央后备警察部队，中央工业警察部队，边境卫队等也用于中央邦，马哈拉施特拉邦，拉贾斯坦邦，喀拉拉邦，贾坎德邦，恰蒂斯加尔邦等国家警察部队。

蒂鲁吉拉帕利军械厂（OFT），也称为特里奇军械厂，是由印度先进[武器](https://news.163.com/news/search?keyword=%E6%AD%A6%E5%99%A8)和设备有限公司经营的小型武器工厂，总部设在泰米尔纳德邦蒂鲁吉拉帕利，以前是印度政府国防部军械厂委员会的一部分。 公司由一名称为总经理的国防部军械厂委员会官员领导，他是首席执行官，负责公司的整体管理。 该军械厂是印度最大的小型武器制造公司，拥有最广泛的轻武器生产范围。

 它于1966年7月3日由当时的印度总理英迪拉·甘地揭幕，并于1967年开始生产。设立该厂是为了增加该国的[轻武器](https://news.163.com/news/search?keyword=%E8%BD%BB%E6%AD%A6%E5%99%A8)生产，协助坎普尔的伊沙波尔步枪厂。

 其实印度不好高骛远，认准一种轻武器，吃透也是没什么问题的。造出来不会那么多问题。

口径7.62，发射7.62*39弹药，弹匣是工程塑料的。可以使用ak47 akm[弹匣](https://news.163.com/news/search?keyword=%E5%BC%B9%E5%8C%A3)。

**New Delhi: A high-tech, low sound carbine named ‘TriCa’ with a range more effective than a typical sub-machine gun and small enough to be packed in the jacket of security personnel was unveiled at the Ordnance Factory in Tiruchirappalli, Tamil Nadu.**

[![Image 9: ads](https://raksha-anirveda.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/kalyani_banner.jpg)](https://www.kssl.in/)

The lighter and compact weapon, the 7.62X39 mm carbine TriCa is designed for the infantry combat vehicle, helicopter crew and security personnel for operations that call for a compact and relatively powerful individual automatic weapon.

The weapon is also for paratroopers, police and security personnel guarding highly secure facilities such as airports, and for use by the Special Operation Forces, a defence press release here said.

TriCa has a special muzzle booster which helps in hiding the flash and mitigating the sound when fired, the release said. An advantage is that it can use ammunition and magazines as well as the inter-changeable parts of general assault rifles (TAR and AK-47).

The carbine could be concealed in clothes and hidden in jackets of security personnel. It was developed by the in-house research and development unit of the Ordnance Factory.

[![Image 7: Sandeep Unnithan](https://akm-img-a-in.tosshub.com/indiatoday/images/reporter/201901/image005_0-770x433-profile_image_one_to_one_1.jpg?VersionId=.pasKkvdD84ULmLha3vENVAV69BnJMOd&size=50:50)](https://www.indiatoday.in/author/sandeep-unnithan "Sandeep Unnithan")

![Image 8: Logo for India Today Magazine Insight](https://akm-img-a-in.tosshub.com/indiatoday/images/mediamanager/india_today_insight.jpg?IzvocAu7gyMv.UA3nBmTl5xRnm990vx3)It’s laptop-sized, can be carried inside a coat and can spit AK-47 bullets out at the rate of roughly 700 rounds per minute. Meet the ‘Baby TAR’, India’s smallest assault rifle. Developed by the Indian Ordnance Factory Tiruchirappali, the weapon is a compact version of the legendary AK-47, which the factory has been mass-producing since 2017. This in-house OFB innovation comes soon after the Indian Army unveiled a 9x19mm carbine developed in-house.

advertisement

The TAR-3, a compact, fully automatic version of the Trichy Assault Rifle (TAR), recently passed a series of trials at the Ordnance Factory Trichy (OF Trichy). A dozen prototypes have been produced during the lockdown. The weapon is currently undergoing ‘unofficial trials’ with the Indian Army, where three prototypes are believed to have fired over 2,000 rounds each without stoppages.

The ‘Baby TAR’ fires the same 7.62x39 mm cartridge as the AK-47—this ammunition is in widespread production and use, thereby easing logistics. It uses the AK-47’s distinctive 30-round curved box magazine and features a commonality of parts with existing weapons. Its designers chopped down the AK-47’s 16-inch barrel, producing a weapon with an 8.3-inch barrel and an effective range of 150 metres. The TAR-3 is 19.2 inches long with its stock folded, and at 2.7 kg (unloaded), is one kg lighter than the AK-47. It has a monoblock receiver, shockproof polymer lower parts and two Picatinny rails that can mount a variety of sights and scopes.

ALSO READ | [The Indian Army’s ‘General Kalashnikov’ gives it a new 9 mm sub-machine gun](https://www.indiatoday.in/india-today-insight/story/the-indian-army-s-general-kalashnikov-gives-it-a-new-9-mm-sub-machine-gun-1759202-2021-01-14)

Its designers say it is ideal for users like special forces and counter-terrorist operators who want compact, concealable weapons but with the firepower of a full-sized AK-47. The assault rifle is also suitable for aircraft, tank and vehicle crews. Significantly, the weapon was developed as an unsolicited design—without waiting for army General Staff Qualitative Requirements (GSQRs), which usually is the start point for weapon development. To do so, the factory used the experience it gained from mass producing the Trichy Assault Rifle, a wholly indigenous copy of the AK-47.

Designers at OF Trichy appear to have solved a problem that stumped the gun designers of the DRDO’s now-discarded INSAS carbine variant in the 1990s—how to reduce the barrel heating and the excessive sound and flash produced when an assault rifle bullet is fired from a short barrel. The DRDO did it by switching over to a smaller bullet, the 5.56x30 round used in the JVPC carbine. The Baby TAR designers solved the problem by used internal metal reflectors to insulate the foregrip from the barrel and by designing, in-house, a compact flash hider at the barrel muzzle. The gun can presently fire four full magazines—around 120 rounds—without the barrel heating. This development is noteworthy because it means Indian designers now understand the ‘know-why’, rather than just the ‘know-how’ that they would have gained from a licensed production.

advertisement

**Compacting the AK**

The Soviet Union began producing compact, stubbier versions of its AK-74 rifle (an AK-47 evolution firing the 5.45x39 mm cartridge) in the 1970s. Copies of this compact assault rifle have been famously attached to Osama bin Laden, ISIS chief Abu Bakr Al Baghdadi and more recently, Belarus President Alexander Lukashenko. Compact versions of the AK-47 believed to have been produced in the frontier regions of Pakistan, have been recovered by Indian security forces from terrorists in Jammu and Kashmir in recent months.

Trichy is one of two Indian ordnance factories already mass-producing Indian versions of the legendary Kalashnikov (the original weapon was never patented and is freely made by countries across the world). The ‘Ghatak’, a copy made by Rifle Factory Ishapore, did not find as much favour. The full-sized TAR is believed to be a copy of the Bulgarian AR-M1, itself a licensed copy of the Kalashnikov. Over 500,000 Bulgarian weapons have been imported by India’s central, state and paramilitary forces over the past decade—the TAR, which began bulk production in 2017, has also helped reducing imports from that east European country. OF Trichy has developed four variants of the rifle, with fixed, side-folding, under-folding and telescoping butts. Nearly 20,000 weapons have been delivered to the Indian police, paramilitary and central armed police forces. Interestingly, each TAR costs around Rs 55,000—far less than the licensed AK-203 to be produced by Indo-Russian Rifles, which will cost upwards of Rs 75,000. And the compact version could cost less than the full-length TAR.

advertisement

The compact TAR’s arrival has added to growing numbers of indigenously designed small arms. From a virtual drought a few years back, there are now multiple indigenous designs available, chambered for various cartridges. Besides the Army’s 9x19mm carbine, the DRDO has developed a variant firing a 5.56x45 mm cartridge, for a different Army requirement. The JVPC, a DRDO-OFB carbine, passed Army and MHA development trials last year. Bengaluru-based small arms start up SSS Defence has its own designs for weapons, chambered for 5.56x45 and 7.62x39 cartridges, and an upgrade kit for existing AK-47 variants. All these designs, of course, are at the prototype stage and will need to fire several thousand rounds before they are fit for mass-production and induction.

While the Indian army has been looking for foreign assault rifles such as the Sig Sauer 716 and the AK-203 to meet its needs, paramilitary forces such as the CRPF and state police have been aggressively acquiring indigenously developed assault rifles such as the TAR or Trichy assault rifle, TriCa – the carbine version of the TAR, and the Ishapore Assault Rifle.

![Image 1: TAVOR: Reliable Firepower Of Indian Special Forces »](https://i0.wp.com/www.defencexp.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/1079001857_0_0_2994_1684_1200x0_80_0_1_eb8bced5593bd965e8ebefbc587a5cec.jpg?resize=1024%2C576&ssl=1)

Trichy Assault Rifle & Ghatak have already been integrated into the CRPF’s service, and in February 2022, they became the first users of the 7.62X51mm Ishapore Assault Rifle. We recently reported that Delhi Police has placed a big order for 5000 carbines for Rs 85 crores with Joint Venture Protective Carbine (JVPC). NSG has also placed an order for 100 Trica carbines for December 2021.

In terms of TAR, OFT has provided around 10,000 rifles to Central Armed Police Forces as as the BSF, SSB, ITBP, and CISF. TAR has also been incorporated into the police force of numerous states as part of their modernisation programme. OFT has a monthly output rate of 2000 TAR. The Central Armed Police Forces’ faith in the assault rifle points to its success.

While OFT is preparing to execute a 100-unit order for the TriCa compact carbine, states dealing with Naxals were eager to arm their forces with the 7.72×39 mm weapon.

![Image 2: Jammu & Kashmir News 🇮🇳 on Twitter: "OFB TRICHY Launches 7.62X39mm Carbine  (#TriCa), developed through in house R&D of Ordnance Factory  Tiruchirappalli -TriCa is a lighter and compact weapon. TriCa is designed](https://pbs.twimg.com/media/E7ek3j5UcAEG3Jk.jpg)

Out of the orders for 78,000 guns placed collectively by the Central Reserve Police Force, Border Security Force, Sashastra Seema Bal, and police forces in States, OFT has delivered 30,000 Tiruchi Assault Rifle (TAR) and will supply 42,000 to 45,000 units during this fiscal.

### **Recent TAR and TriCa orders**

According to an unclassified report recently provided by the Department of Defense, on February 12th, the CRPF placed a large order for 10,000 TAR costing 76.48 crore with Advance Weapons & Equipment India Limited (AWEIL). On the 31st of January 2022, AWEIL received another modest order from Kerela Police for 92 TriCa carbines costing 67.16 crore.
